question.title: Fundamental Pillars of Object-Oriented Programming
question.statement: Which of the following concepts constitute the core foundational pillars of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)? (Select all that apply)
question.explanation: The four classic pillars of OOP are Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, and Polymorphism. Paging is an Operating System virtual memory management concept.

question.title: Read Phenomena Prevented by Serializable Isolation
question.statement: Which of the following concurrency read anomalies are completely prevented under standard ANSI SQL Serializable isolation level? (Select all that apply)
question.explanation: Serializable isolation is the highest ANSI SQL isolation level and eliminates Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, and Phantom Reads. Hardware disk failures are addressed by Durability/storage replication, not concurrency control.

question.title: Prime Numbers in Specified Interval
question.statement: Which of the following integers are prime numbers located strictly between 20 and 30? (Select all that apply)
question.explanation: Between 20 and 30: 21 is divisible by 3 and 7; 23 is prime; 27 is divisible by 3 and 9; 29 is prime. The prime numbers are 23 and 29.

question.title: Python List Mutability
question.statement: In standard CPython, built-in `list` objects are mutable data structures that can have elements modified, appended, or removed in-place without creating a new list object.
question.explanation: Python lists are mutable sequences. Operations like `append()`, `extend()`, `pop()`, and item assignment modify the existing list object in-place in memory.

question.title: HTTP/1.1 Application-Layer Multiplexing Capability
question.statement: HTTP/1.1 natively supports full concurrent request/response multiplexing over a single TCP connection without suffering from application-layer Head-of-Line (HoL) blocking.
question.explanation: HTTP/1.1 requires pipelined requests to be responded to in exact sequential arrival order, causing application-layer Head-of-Line blocking. True binary stream multiplexing over a single TCP connection was introduced in HTTP/2.

question.title: Gregorian Calendar Century Leap Year Rule
question.statement: In the standard Gregorian calendar, century years (such as 1900, 2000, 2100) are leap years if and only if they are evenly divisible by 400.
question.explanation: Under the Gregorian calendar rule, a century year is a leap year only if it is divisible by 400. Thus, 2000 was a leap year, whereas 1900 and 2100 are not leap years.

question.title: Simple Interest Accrual Calculation
question.statement: Calculate the total Simple Interest (in dollars) accrued on a principal investment of $1,000 at an annual interest rate of 5% over a period of exactly 3 years.

question.title: Right Triangle Hypotenuse Length
question.statement: In a Euclidean right-angled triangle, the lengths of the two perpendicular legs are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse in centimeters?
question.explanation: According to the Pythagorean theorem: Hypotenuse = sqrt(a² + b²) = sqrt(6² + 8²) = sqrt(36 + 64) = sqrt(100) = 10 cm.

question.title: Count of Structurally Unique Binary Trees for N Nodes
question.statement: How many structurally unique binary search trees (BSTs) can be constructed using exactly 3 distinct keys?
question.explanation: The number of structurally unique BSTs that can be formed with n distinct nodes is given by the nth Catalan Number C_n = (2n)! / ((n + 1)! * n!). For n = 3: C_3 = (6)! / (4! * 3!) = 720 / (24 * 6) = 720 / 144 = 5.

question.title: ANSI SQL Three-Valued Logic NULL Equality Evaluation
question.statement: In standard ANSI SQL, what is the resulting boolean truth value of evaluating the predicate expression `NULL = NULL` in a WHERE filter?

options.text: UNKNOWN (evaluates to non-true, filtering out rows)

question.explanation: SQL operates on Three-Valued Logic (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN). A NULL represents an unknown missing value, so comparing any value (even another NULL) using '=' yields UNKNOWN. In WHERE clauses, only predicates that evaluate strictly to TRUE are retained; UNKNOWN evaluates to falsey for filtering. To test for NULL, `IS NULL` must be used.
